title: external-subagent MCP public API
description: The intentionally small external_subagent_* wire catalog.

effort_selection.description: Reasoning-effort steering capability. All agents forward the token to their target runtime.

subagent_models_status.description: Passive projection of recorded model-catalog evidence. Present only when discovery ever ran (status probe=true or an explicit models call); never discovered means the field is absent. Recorded evidence whose config revision no longer matches degrades to supported=false with reason stale_config_revision.

tokens.description: Model selection tokens usable verbatim in spawn model (zcode provider/model, dsh provider:model, codex model id, agy bare slug). Empty when supported is false.

source.description: Evidence source label, e.g. zcode_session_create_settings, codex_app_server_model_list, dsh_acp_models_list, agy_models_list.

version.description: Runtime version observed at discovery time; omitted when unknown.

checked_at_ms.description: Epoch milliseconds when the evidence was recorded.

reason.description: Bounded degradation reason (stale_config_revision, auth_required, model_catalog_empty, transport, ...); omitted on success.

subagent_scope_status.description: Readiness conclusion only. Probe evidence (scope paths, version, checked_at_ms, reason) stays on the daemon RPC view for the CLI diagnose owner.

spawn.description: Start one new durable subagent in an absolute repository with a complete bounded prompt. A successful call establishes a session and returns agent_id, session_id and status; it does not mean the assignment is finished. Use a named profile or explicit runtime settings, never both. Every successful spawn creates a new task. Read the complete response before continuing; preserve any returned actor identity on failure instead of blindly spawning again. Use external_subagent_wait with the actual agent_id to collect completion in this turn; do not replace waiting with automatic wake-up and ending the turn.

profile.description: Profile name referencing a JSON preset in profiles/*.json. Mutually exclusive with subagent, permission_mode, model, effort, and developer_instructions.

subagent.description: Subagent route key; omission uses configured default_subagent or returns subagent_required. Null is invalid; dsh production spawn requires its enabled + spawn_supported + pinned-runtime configuration.

permission_mode.description: codex supports build/edit (workspace-write), plan (read-only), and yolo (danger-full-access), always with approvalPolicy=never; agy supports only build (--mode accept-edits) and yolo (--dangerously-skip-permissions).

model.description: Task model. dsh requires provider:model, split at the first colon (the model side may contain further colons; a missing colon or an empty side is rejected before any task). codex uses its own model id; zcode requires an explicit provider/model token from the spawn request or a named profile, and rejects a bare token, an omitted model, and agents.zcode.default_model at admission. agy uses its native model token. The target runtime validates the selection. Omission falls back to the configured default_model for dsh and agy, then to the provider-native model; codex requires an explicit model or agents.codex.default_model; zcode and codex never fall back to a provider default.

effort.description: Optional reasoning-effort token passed to the target runtime.

developer_instructions.description: Per-task developer instructions (at most 1 MiB). codex routes them through the native developerInstructions channel on thread/start (prompt stays verbatim); every other subagent splices them as a 'Developer Instructions:' prefix block ahead of the prompt. A trimmed-empty string means not provided (no admission effect). Mutually exclusive with profile: profiles carry their own developer_instructions. The spliced prompt stays under the shared 256 KiB prompt bound, which rejects the spawn before task creation; oversized developer_instructions are themselves rejected with validation before any task.

write_manifest.description: codex requires an empty or omitted write_manifest; non-empty input returns codex_write_manifest_unsupported before task creation. agy likewise requires an empty or omitted write_manifest; non-empty input returns agy_write_manifest_unsupported before task creation. dsh admits a non-empty manifest in build through the guarded manifest-build composition (workspace-write sandbox, only tool-fs writable, out-of-manifest paths rejected as FS_WRITE_MANIFEST_DENIED), at most 256 entries; an explicit ["."] keeps the existing build composition. plan requires an empty manifest for every subagent.

list.description: List tasks for the required absolute repository path. Pass repository, not scope; subagent, phase and outcome are optional filters.

wait.description: Wait for persistent task progress. agent_id accepts one number or an array of 1..16 ids; wait_time is seconds, 0..600 (default 290). wait_mode=all (default) waits for all known targets to become terminal; any wakes when one is terminal, enabling rolling replacement. An actionable pending request also wakes either mode. Scalar waits behave identically in both modes. Remove already-terminal ids from subsequent any waits. Unknown ids do not count as terminal. Waiting or cancelling the wait does not cancel tasks. Scalar input returns one wait object; array input returns a flat object keyed by agent id, plus error markers for duplicated or unknown_agent ids. Repeated ids are awaited once. message_id is supported only with scalar input. Read the complete output in the caller context; do not truncate or select fields in a wrapper. result=null means no final result yet. timed_out means this wait's deadline expired, not that the task failed; early any wakes leave still-running peers timed_out=false. Only outcome=COMPLETED is success. Read final_text, preserve failure_message, and follow next_offset with result until null; for a native turn failure, final_text contains the complete original error as JSON with credentials redacted, while failure_message carries bounded ES diagnostics, the embedded page is complete when next_offset=null. failure_message is a bounded diagnostic string, usually JSON: parse defensively, read the original cause separately from cleanup_result, and decide continuation or retry from the actual failure. Do not immediately retry persistent quota/authentication failures. Handle permission requests with allow/deny and user-input requests by answering their full embedded question. Activity provides incremental latest_text_tail, latest_text_truncated, tool_calls_last_60s, telemetry_status, last_activity_age_ms, model_request_active, in_flight_tool_count and oldest_in_flight_tool_age_ms. activity.model_activity is present only when the native source provided a model-activity fact: it carries that native phase (started/completed/failed/retry_scheduled/stream_stalled) and any native retry detail; no wait age or attempt count is invented, and a retry wait is not a degraded task. activity.diagnostics is a bounded summary (at most 32 entries) of deduplicated anomalous native inputs: source protocol, closed disposition reason, affected dimensions (known or unknown scope), safe discriminator, occurrence count, and last-observed epoch milliseconds; activity.diagnostics_truncated marks entries folded into a summary_limit record. An empty list means no known anomaly, not that observation is complete; repeated waits neither recompute nor increment counts. These are liveness evidence, not proof of success; zero tracked tools can also mean unsupported tracking. Ordinary progress and message receipts do not wake a wait. Use observe only when the activity suggests a stuck task or meaningless loop.

agent_id.description: One agent id (scalar response) or a list of 1..=16 ids awaited together (response is an object keyed by agent id, each value the ordinary wait output or {"error":"duplicated"}/{"error":"unknown_agent"}).

message_id.description: Only supported with a scalar agent_id.

wait_mode.description: all waits for every task; any wakes on one terminal task. Pending requests wake both. Scalar waits behave identically.

observe.description: Read captured task observations for any subagent. Exposes at most 200 Unicode characters of public reasoning only when a public summary/thought delta was actually observed, labeled with its native protocol/channel; otherwise reasoning is null. recent_calls[].status distinguishes unknown/pending/running/finished/succeeded/failed/cancelled, where unknown means no native phase evidence, finished means ended without success/failure evidence, and succeeded only comes from an explicit native fact. Tool history and coverage follow the actual per-channel evidence, not the configured subagent name. Coverage reports capture gaps and unsupported history truthfully.

result.description: Read a terminal task result. Read outcome before treating final_text as a successful report. On a native turn failure, final_text contains the complete original error as JSON with credentials redacted; failure_message carries bounded ES diagnostics and cleanup outcome. Follow next_offset until null to read the whole original error. Return the complete output to the caller; do not truncate or replace it with selected fields. The result keeps its stable outcome and partial status. Returns null result while the task is non-terminal. A failed terminal result also carries failure_message: usually the daemon's bounded single-line JSON failure detail, but an early fail_claim row may be plain text, so treat it as an opaque bounded string and attempt JSON parsing defensively (null when the task has no persisted detail or the outcome is not a failure). Questions from user-input requests are embedded in full in external_subagent_wait projections, not paged here.

question_projection.description: Embedded question of an answerable user-input request in the wait projection's pending_requests entries; wait is the only retrieval surface, so a question beyond the embed cap is marked truncated instead of paged.

native_error.description: Complete credential-redacted native error for a synchronous native command failure. `original` is authoritative and complete; it is null only when `truncated` is true, and the object then reports total_bytes/limit_bytes instead of claiming delivery. `projection` only carries native meaning the source stated explicitly.

external_subagent_wait.output_many: <agent_id> keys, "error" only when an id was duplicated or unknown
external_subagent_wait.parallel_note: spawn all subagents first, then wait once with the full id list

activity_diagnostic_projection.description: One bounded, already-sanitized diagnostic summary entry from the retained common state. `reason` is the closed disposition vocabulary (unknown_semantics, malformed, truncated, dropped, permission_denied, auxiliary_terminal, retention_limit, summary_limit); `discriminator` is a safe native method/type token, never a payload. `count` counts deduplicated native inputs, not derived facts or wait repetitions.

impact.description: known lists the affected coverage dimensions; unknown asserts uncertainty rather than loss in any specific dimension.
